No — sloths live in the rainforests of Central and South America. Here, you'll only find them in some zoos, not our forests.

Wala — nakatira ang sloth sa mga kagubatan ng Gitna at Timog Amerika. Dito, makikita lang sila sa ilang zoo, hindi sa ating kagubatan.

Soap drags and wraps germs and dirt so water washes them away! Alcohol kills microbes by breaking them apart, but it can't remove visible dirt.

Bakit mas maganda ang sabon kaysa alcohol kapag kitang-kita ang dumi sa kamay?

Hinihila at binabalot ng sabon ang germ at dumi para mahugasan ng tubig! Pinapatay ng alcohol ang mikrobyo sa pamamagitan ng pagsira sa kanila, pero hindi nito tinatanggal ang nakikitang dumi.

Ngano nga mas maayo ang sabon kaysa alcohol kon kitakita ang hugaw sa kamot?

Birahon ug putoson sa sabon ang germ ug hugaw aron mahugasan sa tubig! Mopatay ang alcohol sa mikrobyo pinaagi sa pagguba kanila, apan dili niini matangtang ang makita nga hugaw.

How does soap clean our dirty clothes?

Soap grabs the oil and dirt, loosening the grime from the cloth! Then, it lets the water easily carry all that dirt away.

Paano nililinis ng sabon ang ating mga maruming damit?

Hinahagip ng sabon ang langis at dumi, pinapakawalan ito sa damit! Pagkatapos, hinahayaan nito na dalhin ng tubig ang lahat ng dumi palayo.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglimpyo sa sabon sa atong hugaw nga mga sinina?

Gikupot sa sabon ang lana ug hugaw, gipakawala kini gikan sa sanina! Dayon, tugotan niini nga dad-on sa tubig ang tanang buling palayo.

Ilang gramo ng sodium ang nasa isang mole ng table salt (NaCl)?

Mayroong 22.99 gramo ng sodium. Ito ay dahil ang atomic mass ng sodium ay 22.99 g, at ang isang mole ng isang elemento ay may ganoong mass sa gramo!
copy.bis:
Pila ka gramo sa sodium ang anaa sa usa ka mole sa table salt (NaCl)?

Adunay 22.99 gramo sa sodium. Kini tungod kay ang atomic mass sa sodium kay 22.99 g, ug ang usa ka mole sa usa ka elemento adunay ingon niana nga mass sa gramo!

copy.bis:

I-arrange ang V = BvL aron makuha ang L: L = V ÷ (B × v) = 6 ÷ (0.5 × 6) = 2 metros!

copy.bis: Ang sound mobiyahe og mga 1005 metros kada segundo sa helium sa 0°C ug mga 1300 metros kada segundo sa hydrogen sa 20°C, pareho nga mas paspas kaysa sa ordinaryong hangin.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound can travel not only through air but also through solid materials like a string
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sound traveling through solids, a physics topic. G6-M-6 is about separating mixtures (decantation, winnowing, etc.), which is unrelated to sound transmission.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound can travel not only through air but also through solid materials like a string
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the benefits of each mixture separation technique in preparing useful products
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sound traveling through solids, a physics topic. G6-M-7 is about benefits of mixture separation techniques, which is unrelated to sound transmission.

copy.en: Sound can travel not only through air but also through solid materials like a string, which carries the vibrations from one cup to another.
copy.tl: Ang tunog ay hindi lang dumadaan sa hangin kundi pati na rin sa mga solidong materyales tulad ng tali, na nagdadala ng vibration mula sa isang tasa papunta sa isa pa.
copy.bis: Ang tingog dili lang moagi sa hangin kondili sa mga solidong materyales usab sama sa pisi, nga nagdala sa vibration gikan sa usa ka tasa ngadto sa lain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Human activities like burning fuels, cutting down forests, and making certain products release extra greenhouse gases that strengthen the greenhouse effect.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses greenhouse gas emissions from human activities and the greenhouse effect. G6-M-4 requires describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures (solutions and suspensions). There is no connection to mixtures, solutions, or suspensions; the content is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en: Human activities like burning fuels, cutting down forests, and making certain products release extra greenhouse gases that strengthen the greenhouse effect.
copy.tl: Ang mga gawain ng tao tulad ng pagsunog ng fuels, pagputol ng mga kagubatan, at paggawa ng ilang produkto ay naglalabas ng karagdagang greenhouse gases na nagpapalakas sa greenhouse effect.
copy.bis: Ang mga kalihokan sa tawo sama sa pagsunog og fuels, pagputol sa mga kalasangan, ug paghimo sa pipila ka produkto nagpagawas og dugang nga greenhouse gases nga nagpalig-on sa greenhouse effect.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Common sound sources include people, animals, nature, household objects, and electronics.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe the possible effects of human activities, such as deforestation, pollution, and introduction of invasive species, on living things in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sources of sound, a physics topic, and provides no information about the effects of human activities (deforestation, pollution, invasive species) on living things in an ecosystem. It does not support the competency in any way.

copy.en: Sources of sound include musical instruments, electronic devices, and natural sounds like birds singing or thunder rumbling.
copy.tl: Kabilang sa mga pinagmumulan ng tunog ang mga instrumentong pangmusika, electronic devices, at natural sounds tulad ng pag-awit ng mga ibon o pagdagundong ng kulog.
copy.bis: Ang mga tinubdan sa tingog naglakip sa mga instrumento sa musika, electronic devices, ug natural sounds sama sa pag-awit sa mga langgam o pagdahunog sa dalugdog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why do animals need space?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why animals need space to find food, water, and live with others. The competency G5-E-11 requires describing the general structure of the solar system, celestial objects, and their features/composition. The card content is entirely unrelated to the solar system.

copy.en:
Why do animals need space?

Space gives them enough area to find food and water, and to move, play, and live with others without fighting too much.
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangan ng mga hayop ang space?

Ang space ay nagbibigay sa kanila ng sapat na lugar para maghanap ng pagkain at tubig, at para gumalaw, maglaro, at mamuhay kasama ang iba nang hindi masyadong nag-aaway.
copy.bis:
Nganong ang mga mananap nagkinahanglan ug space?

Ang space naghatag kanila ug igong lugar aron mangita sa pagkaon ug tubig, ug aron molihok, magdula, ug mopuyo uban sa uban nga dili kaayo mag-away.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The spaces between particles in a solid are very small
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes particle spacing in solids, a matter/particle model concept. G6-E-8 is about constructing a Sun-Earth-Moon model to explain seasons, star patterns, and eclipses. There is no connection to the assigned competency.

copy.en: The spaces between particles in a solid are very small, which is why solids are hard to compress or squeeze.
copy.tl: Napakaliit ng mga espasyo sa pagitan ng mga particle sa solid, kaya mahirap i-compress o pisilin ang mga solid.
copy.bis: Gamay kaayo ang mga espasyo tali sa mga particle sa solid, mao nga lisod i-compress o pisliton ang mga solid.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Specific heat capacity is the amount of heat needed to change the temperature of a substance by one degree
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines specific heat capacity, a physics/thermodynamics concept. It provides no information about grouping animals by the food they eat (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Specific heat capacity is the amount of heat needed to change the temperature of a substance by one degree
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw a simple food chain using living things from the Philippines and label them as herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about specific heat capacity and does not support drawing a food chain of Philippine living things labeled as herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores.

copy.en: Specific heat capacity is the amount of heat needed to change the temperature of a substance by one degree, and every substance has its own value.
copy.tl: Ang specific heat capacity ay ang dami ng heat na kailangan para baguhin ang temperatura ng isang bagay ng isang degree, at bawat bagay ay may sariling halaga nito.
copy.bis: Ang specific heat capacity mao ang gidaghanon sa heat nga gikinahanglan aron mausab ang temperatura sa usa ka butang ug usa ka degree, ug ang matag butang adunay kaugalingong bili.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They fuse together! This joining is called fertilization
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the changes of state in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes: a. solid → liquid → vapor, and b. vapor → liquid → solid
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains fertilization (sperm and egg fusing to form the first cell), which is a biological process. G7-M-5 requires explaining changes of state (solid-liquid-vapor) in terms of particle arrangement and energy changes. There is no instructional support for phase changes or particle models.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They fuse together! This joining is called fertilization
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes fertilization, not changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) of solids, liquids, and gases. No diagrams or flowcharts of phase changes are present, and the content is entirely unrelated to matter states.

copy.en:
What happens when a sperm meets an egg?

They fuse together! This joining is called fertilization, and it forms the very first cell of a new organism.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag nagtagpo ang sperm at egg?

Nagsasama sila! Ang pagsasanib na ito ay tinatawag na fertilization, at ito ang bumubuo ng pinakaunang cell ng bagong organismo.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mahitabo kon magkita ang sperm ug egg?

Mag-uban sila! Kini nga paghiusa gitawag ug fertilization, ug kini ang nagporma sa pinakaunang cell sa bag-ong organismo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a spider glues the end of its silk line to a surface first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a spider's anchoring behavior, not the outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) or their roles in movement and food gathering. No body part is mentioned or linked to the competency's skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a spider glues the end of its silk line to a surface first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a spider's immediate anchoring behavior, not an example of animals changing to better suit their environment (e.g., mimicry or camouflage). It does not address adaptation or evolutionary change.

copy.en: Before it drops down, a spider glues the end of its silk line to a surface first, so it has a firm anchor to hang from.
copy.tl: Bago bumaba, idinidikit muna ng gagamba ang dulo ng sinulid nito sa isang ibabaw, para may matibay itong kapitan.
copy.bis: Sa dili pa manaog, ipapilit una sa lawalawa ang tumoy sa iyang hilo sa usa ka bawon, aron adunay lig-on nga kapyotan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its starting speed splits into two parts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: determine how forces can change the shape of objects such as when they are pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, or squeezed
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches resolving initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components for projectile motion. G4-F-6 is about how forces change the shape of objects (pushed, pulled, stretched, bent, twisted, squeezed). The card has no relation to shape changes caused by forces and belongs to a much higher grade level (projectile motion).

copy.en: When you launch something at an angle, its starting speed splits into two parts: v0x = v0 cos θ for sideways motion and v0y = v0 sin θ for upward motion.
copy.tl: Kapag inihagis mo ang isang bagay nang may anggulo, nahahati ang panimulang bilis nito sa dalawang bahagi: v0x = v0 cos θ para sa pahalang na galaw at v0y = v0 sin θ para sa paitaas na galaw.
copy.bis: Kung ilabay nimo ang usa ka butang nga may anggulo, mabahin ang sinugdanan nga kusog sa duha ka parte: v0x = v0 cos θ para sa pahigda nga lihok ug v0y = v0 sin θ para sa paitaas nga lihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Around March 20, the Sun's direct rays hit the equator
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use local information or other reliable sources to identify where the nearest active and inactive volcanoes are located and assess the risk of impacts from eruptions to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the spring equinox and equal day/night lengths. It contains no information about locating active or inactive volcanoes, assessing eruption risk, or local volcanic hazards.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Around March 20, the Sun's direct rays hit the equator
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe some of the materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses the equinox and seasons, not materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines.

copy.en:
Why do day and night feel equal in March?

Around March 20, the Sun's direct rays hit the equator, so every place on Earth gets about 12 hours of day and 12 hours of night. This starts spring in the Northern Hemisphere!
copy.tl:
Bakit parang pantay ang araw at gabi tuwing Marso?

Sa bandang Marso 20, ang direktang sinag ng Araw ay tumatama sa equator, kaya ang bawat lugar sa Earth ay nakakakuha ng halos 12 oras ng araw at 12 oras ng gabi. Ito ang simula ng spring sa Northern Hemisphere!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga morag parehas ang adlaw ug gabii sa Marso?

Sa mga Marso 20, ang direktang silaw sa Adlaw moigo sa equator, busa ang matag lugar sa Earth makakuha og halos 12 ka oras nga adlaw ug 12 ka oras nga gabii. Kini ang sinugdanan sa spring sa Northern Hemisphere!

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes developmental stages of living things, which is unrelated to the Sun-Earth-Moon system model, seasons, star patterns, or eclipses required by G6-E-8.

copy.en: All living things go through a sequence of developmental stages as they grow.
copy.tl: Lahat ng may buhay ay dumadaan sa pagkakasunod-sunod na mga yugto ng pag-unlad habang sila ay lumalaki.
copy.bis: Ang tanang buhing butang moagi sa sunod-sunod nga mga yugto sa paglambo samtang sila modako.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The standard eyepiece on most laboratory microscopes magnifies 10x
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes microscope eyepiece magnification. It contains no information about particles being in motion, having spaces, attracting each other, or moving faster with temperature, which is the subject of G7-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The standard eyepiece on most laboratory microscopes magnifies 10x
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the Particle Model of Matter as 'All matter is made up of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind of particles.'
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about microscope magnification, not about the Particle Model of Matter ('All matter is made up of tiny particles...'). It provides no instructional support for G7-M-2.

copy.en: The standard eyepiece on most laboratory microscopes magnifies 10x, which means it makes the sample look ten times bigger before the objective lens adds its power.
copy.tl: Ang standard na eyepiece sa karamihan ng laboratory microscopes ay nagma-magnify ng 10x, ibig sabihin pinalalaki nito ang sample ng sampung beses bago pa idagdag ng objective lens ang kapangyarihan nito.
copy.bis: Ang standard nga eyepiece sa kadaghanan sa laboratory microscopes nag-magnify ug 10x, nagpasabot nga gipadako kini ang sample ug napulo ka beses sa dili pa idugang sa objective lens ang gahum niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A spectrum is starlight split into rainbow colors!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains star spectra and how color relates to temperature. The competency requires describing the general structure of the solar system, naming major celestial objects, their features, and composition. The card does not address the solar system's structure, planets, or other solar-system objects; it is about stellar spectroscopy, which is outside the scope of this competency.

copy.en:
What is a spectrum and how does it show temperature?

A spectrum is starlight split into rainbow colors! A hot star has more bluish light, while a cool star has more reddish light.
copy.tl:
Ano ang spectrum at paano nito ipinapakita ang temperature?

Ang spectrum ay starlight na hinati sa mga kulay ng bahaghari! Ang mainit na bituin ay may mas maraming bluish light, ang malamig naman ay reddish light.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang spectrum ug giunsa niini pagpakita sa temperature?

Ang spectrum kay starlight nga gipangbahin ngadto sa mga kolor sa bangaw! Ang init nga bituon adunay mas daghang bluish light, ang bugnaw kay reddish light.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Blue stars are the absolute hottest, while red stars are actually cooler!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires describing the general structure of the solar system and identifying major celestial objects (planets, Sun, Moon, etc.) and their features/composition. The card only discusses the colors and relative temperatures of stars, which are not part of the solar system's structure or its major objects. This does not support the competency.

copy.en: Did you know stars have different colors? Blue stars are the absolute hottest, while red stars are actually cooler!
copy.tl: Alam mo ba na iba-iba ang kulay ng mga bituin? Ang mga asul na bituin ang pinakamainit, at ang mga pula naman ang mas malamig!
copy.bis: Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga lahi-lahi ang kolor sa mga bituon? Ang asul nga bituon ang labing init, samtang ang pula mas bugnaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Constellations that are seen all year-round
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about constellations that never set below the horizon, which is astronomy. G4-E-4 requires identifying weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, humidity, rain, and cloud cover. There is no weather content.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Constellations that are seen all year-round
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify evidence of global warming and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses year-round visibility of constellations, not evidence of global warming or climate change. It does not support identifying evidence of global warming and climate change.

copy.en: Constellations that are seen all year-round, like Ursa Major and Cassiopeia, never set below the horizon from our view on Earth.
copy.tl: Ang mga constellation na nakikita sa buong taon, tulad ng Ursa Major at Cassiopeia, ay hindi lumulubog sa horizon mula sa ating paningin sa Earth.
copy.bis: Ang mga constellation nga makita sa tibuok tuig, sama sa Ursa Major ug Cassiopeia, dili mosalop sa horizon gikan sa atong panan-aw sa Earth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It begins with a question or problem
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that a scientific investigation begins with a question or problem. It contains no information about observing or describing the outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) or their roles in movement and food gathering. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en:
Where does a scientific investigation begin?

It begins with a question or problem, often arising because a scientist is curious about something he or she has observed.
copy.tl:
Saan nagsisimula ang isang scientific investigation?

Nagsisimula ito sa isang tanong o problema, na kadalasang lumalabas dahil curious ang scientist sa isang bagay na kanyang na-observe.
copy.bis:
Asa magsugod ang usa ka scientific investigation?

Magsugod kini sa usa ka pangutana o problema, nga sagad mogawas tungod kay curious ang scientist sa usa ka butang nga iyang na-obserbar.

G6-M-1 requires describing changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams and flowcharts. There is no connection to matter or state changes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The equator is the starting point for measuring latitude
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: G6-M-2 requires explaining the role of heat energy in change of state processes. The card is about latitude measurement and the equator, with no mention of heat energy or state changes. Completely unrelated.

copy.en: The equator is the starting point for measuring latitude, and it is read as 0 degrees latitude.
copy.tl: Ang equator ang panimulang punto sa pagsukat ng latitude, at binabasa ito bilang 0 degrees latitude.
copy.bis: Ang equator mao ang sinugdanan nga punto sa pagsukod sa latitude, ug gibasa kini isip 0 degrees latitude.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stay away from glass windows, shelves, cabinets, and other heavy objects during an earthquake because they can break or fall on you.

copy.en: Stay away from glass windows, shelves, cabinets, and other heavy objects during an earthquake because they can break or fall on you.
copy.tl: Lumayo sa mga salaming bintana, estante, cabinet, at iba pang mabibigat na bagay habang lumilindol dahil maaari itong mabasag o bumagsak sa iyo.
copy.bis: Palayo sa mga salamin nga bintana, estante, cabinet, ug uban pang bug-at nga mga butang samtang naglinog kay kini mahimong mabuak o matumba kanimo.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a step-down transformer used in power distribution, which is unrelated to the competency's focus on inferring relationships among current, voltage, and resistance in assembled series and parallel circuits. copy.en: A step-down transformer lowers voltage in distribution lines so electricity can be sent safely to homes.
copy.tl: Ang step-down transformer ay nagpapababa ng voltage sa distribution lines para ligtas na maipadala ang kuryente sa mga tahanan.
copy.bis: Ang step-down transformer nagpaubos sa voltage sa distribution lines aron luwas nga mapadala ang kuryente sa mga panimalay.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about stomach storage, not about particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects on particles. G7-M-3 is a matter/particle model competency and is unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: The stomach is a J-shaped, bag-like muscular organ that can hold about one liter of fluid and food, and its main job is to store food.
copy.tl: Ang tiyan ay isang J-shaped, parang bag na muscular organ na kayang mag-imbak ng halos isang litro ng likido at pagkain, at ang pangunahing trabaho nito ay mag-imbak ng pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang tiyan usa ka J-shaped, sama sa bag nga muscular organ nga makasulod ug mga usa ka litro nga likido ug pagkaon, ug ang pangunang trabaho mao ang pagtipig sa pagkaon.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about a public storm warning signal and expected wind damage, not about properties and uses of metals such as iron, gold, silver, or copper. It is unrelated to G3-M-9.

copy.en: Public Storm Warning Signal 5 means winds of more than 220 kilometers per hour are expected within 12 hours, with very heavy to widespread damage.
copy.tl: Ang Public Storm Warning Signal 5 ay nangangahulugang inaasahan ang hangin na higit 220 kilometers per hour sa loob ng 12 oras, na may napakatindi hanggang malawakang pinsala.
copy.bis: Ang Public Storm Warning Signal 5 nagpasabot nga ang hangin nga labaw sa 220 kilometers per hour gipaabot sa 12 ka oras, nga adunay grabe kaayo hangtod sa lapad nga kadaot.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes stormy weather and safety, with no mention of plate boundaries, their structures, movements, or events. It is unrelated to plate tectonics.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stormy weather brings dark clouds, strong wind, and often heavy rain
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate impacts on the plate above it
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about weather, not about subduction of oceanic plates or its impact on the overriding plate. No tectonic content.

assignedReviews.reason: The card does not identify mountains, faults, volcanoes, or ocean trenches on a map, nor interpret features in relation to plate tectonics. Entirely unrelated.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes stormy weather conditions, which is unrelated to describing biotic and abiotic features of tropical rainforests, swamps, estuaries, mangrove forests, and coral reefs using labeled diagrams.

copy.en: Stormy weather has strong winds, hard rain, a dark sky from thick clouds, lightning, thunder, and cold air.
copy.tl: Ang stormy weather ay may malakas na hangin, malakas na ulan, madilim na langit dahil sa makakapal na ulap, kidlat, kulog, at malamig na hangin.
copy.bis: Ang stormy weather adunay kusog nga hangin, kusog nga ulan, ngitngit nga langit tungod sa baga nga panganod, kilat, dalugdog, ug bugnaw nga hangin.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about linear acceleration, a physics concept. G3-L-7 is about living things depending on one another and the environment. No connection to living things or their basic needs.

copy.en: Linear acceleration happens when an object moves in a straight line and changes speed.
copy.tl: Ang linear acceleration ay nangyayari kapag ang isang bagay ay gumagalaw sa tuwid na linya at nagbabago ang bilis.
copy.bis: Ang linear acceleration mahitabo kung ang usa ka butang molihok sa tul-id nga linya ug magbag-o ang kadasigon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Stretchable objects become longer when pulled
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the parts and functions, and demonstrate proper handling and storing of a compound microscope
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes stretchable vs non-stretchable objects, a physics/materials property. G7-L-1 is about identifying parts and functions of a compound microscope and proper handling/storing. No overlap in content.

copy.en: Stretchable objects become longer when pulled, while non-stretchable objects do not change length when pulled.
copy.tl: Ang mga stretchable na bagay ay humahaba kapag hinihila, habang ang mga non-stretchable na bagay ay hindi nagbabago ng haba kapag hinila.
copy.bis: Ang mga stretchable nga butang molugway kon birahon, samtang ang mga non-stretchable nga butang dili mausab ang gitas-on kon birahon.
